cues.en: Instruction tuning is a powerful and effective technique, but it's not quite good enough to get to
cues.zh: 指令微調很強大、很有效，但還不足以達到

cues.en: the level of human like interactions that you experience when you chat with a modern chatbot like ChatGPT.
cues.zh: 與 ChatGPT 這類現代聊天機器人互動時，那種近似人類的程度。

cues.en: The issue is that all of the methods of training that I've introduced you to so far, like pre-training
cues.zh: 問題是，到目前介紹的預訓練、

cues.en: and fine tuning and instruction tuning, they all rely on a very simple and quantifiable loss function and unsupervised learning.
cues.zh: 微調、指令微調，都依賴非常簡單、可量化的損失函數，以及非監督式學習。

cues.en: But there are qualities of text that we know we like or we know we don't like, but we don't really know how to quantify them mathematically.
cues.zh: 但文字有些特質，我們知道喜不喜歡，卻不知道如何用數學量化。

cues.en: And so therefore the techniques like next token prediction can only take us so far because they cannot
cues.zh: 所以，預測下一個詞元這類技巧，只能帶我們走到某個程度，因為無法

cues.en: be used to get the model to learn patterns that we just don't know how to mathematically specify.
cues.zh: 讓模型學到我們不知道如何用數學明確描述的模式。

cues.en: And that brings us to reinforcement learning from human feedback.
cues.zh: 這就帶到人類回饋強化學習。

cues.en: Now, a complete understanding of how reinforcement learning works is beyond the scope of this course,
cues.zh: 完整理解強化學習超出本課範圍，

cues.en: because it's quite different and quite a bit more complicated than the methods that I'm focusing on in this course.
cues.zh: 因為它與這門課聚焦的方法相當不同，也複雜許多。

cues.en: So instead, in this lecture I'm going to describe RL briefly.
cues.zh: 所以，這堂只簡短介紹 RL，

cues.en: So you have a general understanding of what's involved.
cues.zh: 讓你大致理解涉及什麼。

cues.en: So let me start with the problem.
cues.zh: 先從問題開始。

cues.en: The problem is that although pre-training and fine tuning are really powerful and really effective,
cues.zh: 預訓練與微調雖然強大、有效，

cues.en: they're only able to produce models that can identify and generate patterns that the loss function can mathematically quantify.
cues.zh: 但只能產生辨識與生成那些損失函數能以數學量化之模式的模型。

cues.en: And that's basically things like grammatical accuracy, context appropriateness and so on.
cues.zh: 基本上，就是文法正確性、語境適切性等等。

cues.en: There are qualities of interacting with humans that are just difficult to train into a model using next token prediction.
cues.zh: 但與人互動有些特質，很難用下一詞元預測訓練進模型。

cues.en: For example, when you're talking to an assistant, a human assistant, you want that person to be helpful and kind.
cues.zh: 例如，和人類助理說話，你希望對方樂於助人、友善。

cues.en: You want them to tell you the truth.
cues.zh: 希望對方誠實。

cues.en: You want them to come up with creative solutions that will be useful and so on.
cues.zh: 希望提出有創意、有用的解法，等等。

cues.en: But how can you mathematically describe something like helpfulness or kindness in a simple loss function from one mathematical equation?
cues.zh: 但怎麼用一個簡單損失函數、一條數學方程式，描述有幫助或友善？

cues.en: The answer is you cannot.
cues.zh: 答案是，做不到。

cues.en: These qualities are complex and ill defined.
cues.zh: 這些特質很複雜，定義也不明確。

cues.en: Now who knows, maybe at some point in the future there will be accurate mathematical descriptions of kindness.
cues.zh: 誰知道，也許未來會有精確描述友善的數學方式。

cues.en: But we certainly don't have those now.
cues.zh: 但目前肯定沒有。

cues.en: And even if such a thing were to be possible to describe with equations, it's not clear that it could be implemented at the token level.
cues.zh: 即使能用方程式描述，也不確定是否能在詞元層級實作。

cues.en: For example, kindness is not a quality of the words that come out of your mouth.
cues.zh: 例如，友善不是嘴裡說出的字本身的特質，

cues.en: It's a quality of the kind of emotions that you elicit in other people.
cues.zh: 而是你讓別人產生什麼情緒。

cues.en: The point is that we know what we want when we see it, but next, token prediction just doesn't work that way.
cues.zh: 重點是，看到時知道自己要什麼，但下一詞元預測不是這樣運作。

cues.en: And so all of this means is that we don't really know how to train models to be aligned with human values
cues.zh: 所以，我們其實不知道如何透過非監督式學習，

cues.en: using unsupervised learning and token based loss functions.
cues.zh: 以及以詞元為基礎的損失函數，讓模型對齊人類價值。

cues.en: And yeah, that's what I write here.
cues.zh: 這裡寫的就是這點。

cues.en: The problem is that we don't have a loss function to train models to be aligned with human values and desires and other qualities.
cues.zh: 問題是，沒有能訓練模型對齊人類價值、願望與其他特質的損失函數。

cues.en: These are the kinds of issues that reinforcement learning from human feedback is designed to solve.
cues.zh: 人類回饋強化學習，就是為了解決這類問題。

cues.en: Very broadly, the idea is to give humans multiple generated outputs from a model and have them state which one they prefer.
cues.zh: 非常概略地說，讓人類看到模型生成的多個輸出，指出偏好哪個。

cues.en: Of course, in the context of LMS, that is two different text versions in response to the same prompt,
cues.zh: 在 LLM 語境中，就是同一提示的兩個不同文字回答，

cues.en: but it could also be two different images, two different pieces of music, or different code that a model produces, whatever the model is generating.
cues.zh: 但也可以是兩張圖、兩段音樂、不同程式碼，或模型生成的任何東西。

cues.en: In fact, you may have seen this yourself when interacting with ChatGPT, where the screen splits and
cues.zh: 事實上，與 ChatGPT 互動時，你可能看過畫面分成兩邊，

cues.en: you get two versions of the same reply, and the website asks you to pick which one of the two you prefer.
cues.zh: 同一回覆有兩個版本，網站請你選擇偏好哪個。

cues.en: If you know what I'm talking about and you've experienced this, then you are actually providing data to OpenAI for them to do reinforcement learning from human feedback.
cues.zh: 如果經歷過，你其實就在為 OpenAI 提供人類回饋強化學習的資料。

cues.en: These preference ratings are used to train llms, to prefer generating token sequences that are associated with what humans state that they prefer.
cues.zh: 這些偏好評分，用來訓練 LLM，讓它傾向生成與人類偏好相關的詞元序列。

cues.en: Well, that sounds nice and very straightforward, but getting humans to read multiple texts and rate
cues.zh: 聽起來很棒、很直接，但讓人讀多段文字、評分

cues.en: their preferences is, you know, that works for small samples, but you need lots and lots of data in many different topic domain areas.
cues.zh: 偏好，小樣本可行，可是我們需要大量資料，涵蓋很多主題領域。

cues.en: So this procedure is very time consuming, quite expensive, and can also be unreliable for several
cues.zh: 所以這非常耗時、昂貴，也可能因為幾個原因

cues.en: reasons that maybe you can probably already think of and which I will describe in the next slide.
cues.zh: 而不可靠；你可能已想到一些，下一張也會說明。

cues.en: So therefore there's even another step of generating a new reward model that is supposed to emulate the average human ratings.
cues.zh: 因此，還有下一步：建立新的獎勵模型，模仿平均人類評分。

cues.en: So that reward model is not the LM that you're training to be a chatbot, but a separate, dedicated
cues.zh: 獎勵模型不是要訓練成聊天機器人的那個 LLM，而是另一個專門、

cues.en: and narrow model that you train to classify texts as ones that humans are likely to prefer or not prefer.
cues.zh: 用途狹窄的模型，用來判斷文字是否可能受到人類偏好。

cues.en: And then that reward model is used to train the LM.
cues.zh: 再用這個獎勵模型訓練 LLM。

cues.en: In the next slide, I'm going to talk about some difficulties and problems with RL If you'd like to
cues.zh: 下一張會討論強化學習的困難與問題。如果想先

cues.en: take a moment to think of some criticisms or issues before I discuss that list, then feel free to pause the video now.
cues.zh: 思考批評或問題，現在可以暫停。

cues.en: Okay, so the first point here is what I've already mentioned.
cues.zh: 好，第一點已經提過。

cues.en: Getting humans to read multiple texts and state which ones they prefer is time consuming, and it's also expensive.
cues.zh: 讓人讀多段文字、指出偏好，耗時，

cues.en: For example, because of labor costs, of course, not everyone agrees on which texts are better.
cues.zh: 也因人力成本而昂貴。當然，不是每個人都同意哪段文字比較好。

cues.en: Some preferences people have are based on personalities or styles that they like, and those preferences can also change over time.
cues.zh: 有些偏好取決於個性、喜歡的風格，也會隨時間改變。

cues.en: They might even change throughout the day.
cues.zh: 甚至一天之內都可能改變。

cues.en: For example, if you're interacting with ChatGPT on a Tuesday morning, maybe you just want the answer to your question because you have a lot of other things to do and you're at work.
cues.zh: 例如，星期二早上在工作、事情很多，與 ChatGPT 互動時，可能只想直接得到答案。

cues.en: But maybe on a Sunday morning you might prefer to have a longer and more detailed interaction, maybe one that's more informal and more time consuming.
cues.zh: 但星期天早上，可能想要更長、更詳細、更隨興，也更花時間的互動。

cues.en: And of course, preferences and values are highly culture dependent.
cues.zh: 當然，偏好與價值也高度依賴文化。

cues.en: There are social, economic, and political topics that people in different countries or different regions
cues.zh: 對某些社會、經濟、政治議題，不同國家、同一國家不同地區，

cues.en: within a country, or even people living in the same home, have very different ideas about.
cues.zh: 甚至同住一個家的人，都可能有很不同的看法。

cues.en: And WRL has a risk of overfitting, just like other forms of training.
cues.zh: RL 和其他訓練方式一樣，有過度擬合風險。

cues.en: But here it is particularly problematic because any biases that the human raters have, even if those
cues.zh: 但這裡特別有問題，因為人類評分者的任何偏見，

cues.en: biases are implicit or unknown to the humans, those are going to be adopted by the model.
cues.zh: 即使是隱含、連自己都不知道的，也可能被模型吸收。

cues.en: And I certainly hope that you agree with me that we do not want these very powerful language models to be racist.
cues.zh: 我希望你同意，我們不想讓這些強大語言模型有種族歧視。

cues.en: We don't want them to be sexist.
cues.zh: 也不想有性別歧視。

cues.en: We don't want them to be bigoted in any way.
cues.zh: 不希望有任何形式的偏狹。

cues.en: But it is extremely easy for models to develop biases against certain groups of people simply because
cues.zh: 但模型很容易對某些群體形成偏見，只因

cues.en: they are trained by human raters who might have implicit or maybe even explicit biases.
cues.zh: 評分者可能有隱含，甚至明顯的偏見。

cues.en: So reinforcement learning from human feedback will simply train the model to generate text that the model thinks the human raters will like.
cues.zh: 所以，人類回饋強化學習，就是訓練模型生成它認為評分者會喜歡的文字。

cues.en: Now, so far, all of these points have just been about variability within and across different human beings giving ratings.
cues.zh: 到目前為止，都在談評分者個人內部，以及不同人之間的變異。

cues.en: But there's also the possibility of humans intentionally giving bad or corrupted data.
cues.zh: 但也可能有人故意提供錯誤或被污染的資料。

cues.en: Perhaps they're doing that because they want to try to sabotage the model training or I don't know, maybe they just think it's funny to give random, unpredictable or junk data.
cues.zh: 也許想破壞訓練，也許只是覺得提供隨機、不可預測、垃圾資料很好玩。

cues.en: Now, I should say here that none of these points listed in this slide are fundamental limitations.
cues.zh: 這裡要說，投影片上的這些點，都不是根本限制。

cues.en: These are challenges that the big AI companies like OpenAI, meta and Microsoft and Google.
cues.zh: 這些是 OpenAI、Meta、微軟、Google 等大型 AI 公司

cues.en: They are actively working to come up with strategies to address these limitations and these issues.
cues.zh: 正在積極研究策略、設法處理的挑戰與問題。

cues.en: But the point is that Rlf is difficult both for theoretical and for practical reasons.
cues.zh: 重點是，RLHF 在理論與實務上都很困難。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: So that is a summary of Rlf.
cues.zh: 這就是 RLHF 的概述。

cues.en: This method has proven to be a really effective tool for getting chatbots to seem more human like.
cues.zh: 這個方法，已證明能有效讓聊天機器人更像人類。

cues.en: Again, you would not need something like this for any application of an LLM for which you have a mathematical
cues.zh: 再次提醒，如果某個 LLM 應用有明確的

cues.en: description of the desired behavior, like accurate classification of a short piece of text.
cues.zh: 目標行為數學描述，例如準確分類短篇文字，就不需要這種做法。

cues.en: Instead, this is a method that is used when the desired characteristics can be qualitatively and subjectively
cues.zh: 它主要用於人類能以質性、主觀方式評估，

cues.en: evaluated by humans, but cannot be easily described mathematically.
cues.zh: 卻難以用數學明確描述的目標特質。
